subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal acceleration formula
explain: Centripetal acceleration always points toward the center; magnitude = v²/r.

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal force on mass m in circular motion
explain: Net inward force required for circular motion is mv²/r.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between linear speed v and angular speed ω
explain: Linear speed equals angular speed times radius of the circular path.

subject: Physics
prompt: Time period T in terms of angular frequency ω
explain: One complete revolution corresponds to angle 2π, so T = 2π/ω.

subject: Physics
prompt: Banking angle θ for frictionless road (speed v, radius r)
explain: On banked frictionless road, normal force components give tan θ = v²/rg.

subject: Physics
prompt: Minimum speed at top of vertical loop to maintain contact
explain: At top, mg provides centripetal force minimally; mv²/r = mg gives v = √(rg).

subject: Physics
prompt: Minimum speed at bottom of vertical loop
explain: Energy conservation from top (v=√rg) to bottom gives v_bottom = √(5rg).

subject: Physics
prompt: Normal force at bottom of vertical circular loop
explain: At bottom, N − mg = mv²/r (both N and centripetal force upward).

subject: Physics
prompt: Normal force at top of vertical circular loop
explain: At top, N + mg = mv²/r; so N = mv²/r − mg.

subject: Physics
prompt: Direction of angular velocity vector (right-hand rule)
explain: ω is an axial vector; direction given by right-hand screw rule along rotation axis.

subject: Physics
prompt: Maximum safe speed on a flat road with friction μ
explain: Friction provides centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r → v = √(μrg).

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal acceleration in terms of T (time period)
explain: v = 2πr/T, so a = v²/r = 4π²r/T².

subject: Physics
prompt: Pseudo force experienced in rotating frame (centrifugal)
explain: In rotating frame, centrifugal pseudo force = mω²r directed radially outward.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle subtended in time t at angular speed ω
explain: For uniform circular motion, angular displacement θ = ωt.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by centripetal force in uniform circular motion
explain: Centripetal force is perpendicular to velocity, so work done is always zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: Tension at angle θ from bottom in vertical circle (speed v)
explain: Radial equation: T − mg cosθ = mv²/r at angle θ from bottom of loop.

subject: Physics
prompt: For uniform circular motion, which quantity is constant?
explain: In UCM, speed and KE are constant; velocity and acceleration directions change continuously.

subject: Physics
prompt: Optimum speed on banked road (with friction μ, angle θ)
explain: At optimum speed, friction is zero; only banking provides centripetal force.

subject: Physics
prompt: Conical pendulum: time period T depends on
explain: For conical pendulum, vertical equilibrium gives T = 2π√(L cosθ/g).

subject: Physics
prompt: In non-uniform circular motion, net acceleration direction
explain: Non-uniform UCM has both centripetal (radial) and tangential components of acceleration.

subject: Physics
prompt: Tangential acceleration in circular motion
explain: Tangential acceleration aₜ = r·α where α is angular acceleration.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between angular acceleration α and linear acceleration aₜ
explain: Just as v = rω, differentiating gives tangential acceleration aₜ = rα.

subject: Physics
prompt: Frequency f and angular speed ω relation
explain: Each cycle covers 2π radians, so ω = 2πf.

subject: Physics
prompt: Height at which particle leaves circular track (inside loop)
explain: Particle leaves when N=0; solving gives h = 5r/3 above ground (bottom of loop).

subject: Physics
prompt: Net force on particle in uniform circular motion
explain: In UCM, |F_net| = mv²/r is constant but direction continuously changes toward center.

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal acceleration in terms of ω and r?
explain: Centripetal acceleration = ω²r, directed toward center.

subject: Physics
prompt: Radius of circular path of charge q in magnetic field B?
explain: Magnetic force provides centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r → r = mv/qB.

subject: Physics
prompt: In vertical circle, speed at top if speed at bottom is v₀?
explain: Energy conservation: ½mv₀² = ½mv_top² + mg(2R) → v_top² = v₀²−4gR.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle swept by radius vector is called?
explain: Angular displacement θ is the angle swept by the radius vector in circular motion.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a particle in uniform circular motion, acceleration is?
explain: Centripetal acceleration is always directed toward center, perpendicular to velocity.

subject: Physics
prompt: Banking angle θ for max safe speed with friction μ on banked road?
explain: Max speed uses friction up the slope: v_max² = rg·tan(θ+φ), φ=arctan(μ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Minimum speed on banked road (friction acting down the slope)?
explain: Below optimum speed, friction acts down slope: v_min² = rg·tan(θ−φ).

subject: Physics
prompt: In a conical pendulum, tension T in the string equals?
explain: Vertical equilibrium: T·cosθ = mg → T = mg/cosθ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Conical pendulum: horizontal component of tension provides?
explain: T·sinθ acts horizontally toward axis, providing the centripetal force mω²r.

subject: Physics
prompt: Angular momentum L of particle in circular motion?
explain: L = r × p; for circular motion, L = mvr (perpendicular r and v).

subject: Physics
prompt: In uniform circular motion, angular momentum is?
explain: No tangential force → no torque → angular momentum remains constant.

subject: Physics
prompt: Centripetal force in terms of angular speed ω?
explain: F = mv²/r and v = ωr → F = mω²r directed toward center.

subject: Physics
prompt: For non-uniform circular motion, tangential force is responsible for?
explain: Tangential force changes the magnitude of velocity (speed), not its direction.

subject: Physics
prompt: Kinetic energy of particle in uniform circular motion is?
explain: Speed is constant in UCM, so KE = ½mv² remains constant throughout.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which physical quantity changes in uniform circular motion?
explain: Velocity (a vector) changes direction continuously; speed and KE remain constant.

subject: Physics
prompt: Radius of curvature of projectile at highest point (initial speed u, angle θ)?
explain: At top, speed = ucosθ; centripetal acc = g → R = v²/g = u²cos²θ/g.

subject: Physics
prompt: Overturning condition for vehicle on flat curve (track width 2d, height h)?
explain: Outer wheel lifts when mv²h/r ≥ mgd, i.e., v² ≥ gd·r/h (for fixed r, d, h).

subject: Physics
prompt: In a rotating frame, centrifugal force on mass m is directed?
explain: Centrifugal (pseudo) force = mω²r acts radially outward in rotating frame.

subject: Physics
prompt: Difference between angular speed of hour and minute hand of clock?

subject: Physics
prompt: Critical velocity at top of vertical loop to just maintain contact?
explain: At top, N=0 → mg = mv²/R → v = √(gR) is the minimum speed.

subject: Physics
prompt: If particle moves in circle of radius r with speed v, its acceleration magnitude?
explain: Centripetal acceleration magnitude = v²/r, always pointing toward center.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between linear velocity v and angular velocity ω in vector form?
explain: v = ω × r; using right-hand rule gives direction tangent to circular path.

subject: Physics
prompt: Net acceleration magnitude in non-uniform circular motion?
explain: Tangential and centripetal accelerations are perpendicular; net = √(aₜ²+ac²).

subject: Physics
prompt: Angle between net acceleration and radius in non-uniform circular motion?
explain: aₜ is perpendicular to ac (radius); angle from radius = tan⁻¹(aₜ/ac).

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle completes n revolutions per second. Its angular speed ω is?
explain: Frequency f = n rev/s; ω = 2πf = 2πn rad/s.
